title: 40 Most Asked React Interview Questions
summary: Forty real React interview questions in ten themed pages, from JSX and state through hooks, reconciliation, performance, Suspense, server components and testing. Each answer gives a short direct answer, key points and a visual.

chapters.title: React Interview Q&A Bank
points: 40 questions in 10 themed pages, 4 per page
Fundamentals first: JSX, components, props, state
Then hooks, keys and reconciliation, context and refs
Then memoization, custom hooks, performance
Then error boundaries, Suspense, server components, testing
Closing cheatsheet of the rules interviewers probe most

chapters.title: JSX and Rendering
points: What is JSX and how does it become JavaScript? (compiles to jsx() calls returning element objects)
What is the virtual DOM and why does React use it? (lightweight element tree diffed to minimize real DOM writes)
What is the difference between rendering and committing? (render phase is pure calculation, commit phase touches the DOM)
Why can't a component return multiple root elements, and what are Fragments? (<>...</> groups children without an extra DOM node)

chapters.title: Components and Props
points: What is the difference between a function component and a class component? (hooks vs lifecycle methods, this binding)
What are props and why are they read-only? (one-way data flow, pure components)
What is the difference between props and state? (props passed in and immutable, state owned and changed by the component)
What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components? (value driven by state vs read from the DOM via ref)

chapters.title: State and useState
points: How does useState work and what does it return? ([value, setter], value is a snapshot per render)
Why is setState asynchronous, and what is batching? (updates queued and applied in one re-render)
What is the difference between setCount(count + 1) and setCount(c => c + 1)? (functional updater avoids stale values)
Why must you never mutate state directly? (same reference means no re-render; copy arrays and objects)

chapters.title: useEffect and Lifecycle
points: How does useEffect map to componentDidMount, DidUpdate and WillUnmount? (dependency array and cleanup function)
What does the dependency array do, and what happens with [], no array, or missing deps? (run once, every render, stale closures)
How do you clean up side effects such as timers, subscriptions and fetches? (return a cleanup, AbortController)
What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect? (after paint vs before paint, flicker and measurement use cases)

chapters.title: Keys and Reconciliation
points: How does React's reconciliation (diffing) algorithm work? (compare by type and position, O(n) heuristics)
Why do lists need keys, and what makes a good key? (stable unique ID that identifies the item)
Why is using array index as a key a problem? (reorder or insert breaks state and input values)
How can changing a key be used to reset a component? (new key means unmount and remount with fresh state)

chapters.title: Context and Refs
points: What is the Context API and what problem does it solve? (avoids prop drilling via Provider and useContext)
What are the performance pitfalls of Context? (all consumers re-render when the value changes; memoize the value, split contexts)
What is useRef and how does it differ from useState? (mutable .current, no re-render on change)
When should you use refs, and what is forwardRef? (focus, measuring, third-party libraries, passing a ref to a child DOM node)

chapters.title: useMemo, useCallback and memo
points: What is the difference between useMemo and useCallback? (caches a computed value vs a function identity)
What does React.memo do and when does it fail? (shallow prop compare, new object or function props break it)
When should you not use useMemo or useCallback? (premature optimization, cost of comparing deps)
What does the React Compiler change about manual memoization? (automatic memoization at build time, fewer hand-written hooks)

chapters.title: Custom Hooks and Performance
points: What is a custom hook and what rules must it follow? (function starting with use that calls other hooks)
What are the Rules of Hooks and why do they exist? (top level only, same call order each render)
How would you find and fix unnecessary re-renders? (React DevTools Profiler, moving state down, memo, stable props)
How do code splitting, lazy and virtualization improve performance? (React.lazy, dynamic import, windowing long lists)

chapters.title: Error Boundaries and Suspense
points: What is an error boundary and what errors does it not catch? (class with getDerivedStateFromError; not event handlers, async code, SSR)
How do you implement a fallback UI and recover from an error? (fallback render, reset key, react-error-boundary)
What is Suspense and how does it work with lazy loading and data? (a component suspends, nearest boundary shows fallback)
What do useTransition and useDeferredValue do? (mark updates non-urgent to keep the UI responsive)

chapters.title: Server Components and Testing
points: What are React Server Components and how do they differ from client components? (run on the server, zero client JS, 'use client' boundary)
What is the difference between SSR, SSG and Server Components? (HTML at request or build time vs components that never ship to the client)
How do you test a React component with React Testing Library? (render, query by role, userEvent, assert behavior not implementation)
How do you test hooks and async behavior? (renderHook, findBy and waitFor, mocking fetch with MSW)

chapters.title: React Interview Cheatsheet
points: Render is pure; side effects belong in effects or event handlers
State: immutable updates, functional updater for dependent changes
useEffect: dependency array rules and cleanup patterns
Keys: stable unique IDs, never the index for dynamic lists
Memoization: measure first, memo + useCallback + useMemo work together
Boundaries: errors, Suspense, 'use client' and what each one covers
